records.title: 4.3L V6 CPI/CSFI "Spider" Fuel Injector Leaks and Poppet Valve Failure
records.description: The 4.3L Vortec V6 used a Central Port Injection system (CPI 1992-1995, CSFI 1996-2002) with a central injector body and six plastic poppet lines — the "spider" — mounted inside the intake manifold. The plastic lines and nut-kit connections crack and leak raw fuel into the plenum, while deposit buildup sticks the poppet valves open or closed, mis-fueling individual cylinders. The result is hard hot starts, persistent misfires, fuel-pressure leak-down, and a rich/fuel-smell condition; GM addressed sticking poppets in TSB 00-06-04-003B by back-servicing the CSFI unit with a redesigned MFI assembly.
records.solution: Replace the spider assembly with the updated GM/Delphi MFI (multi-port) conversion unit, which eliminates the poppet ball-and-seat design, along with the nut kit and upper intake (plenum) gaskets. Fuel-system cleaning sometimes frees sticking poppets temporarily, but replacement is the accepted permanent fix.
symptoms: Hard starting when warm or after sitting overnight
Rough idle and cylinder misfires (P0300-P0306)
Strong fuel smell under the hood
Long crank times from fuel pressure bleed-down
Poor fuel economy and rich running

records.title: 4.3L V6 Lower Intake Manifold Gasket Coolant Leak
records.description: The Vortec 4.3L V6 (like its 5.0L/5.7L siblings) used plastic-carrier lower intake manifold gaskets that erode and crack at the coolant ports from repeated thermal expansion cycles between the aluminum manifold and iron heads. Failures cluster between roughly 80,000 and 150,000 miles, leaking coolant externally at the front or rear of the manifold or internally into the lifter valley, where it contaminates the oil. Left unrepaired, an internal leak destroys bearings and can take out the engine.
records.solution: Replace the lower intake manifold gaskets with the updated metal-carrier 'premium' design gaskets and torque the manifold bolts to spec in sequence. Change the oil afterward if any coolant entered the crankcase.
symptoms: Unexplained coolant loss with no visible puddle
Milky or chocolate-milk colored oil on the dipstick
External coolant seep at the front or rear of the intake manifold
Low coolant light or repeated reservoir top-offs
Sweet coolant smell after shutdown

records.title: 9-Speed Automatic Transmission Shudder
records.description: The 2019+ Blazer with the 9-speed automatic transmission (9T50/9T65) develops a shudder during acceleration from a stop, particularly between 1st and 2nd gear. GM bulletin PIP5608J addresses TCC shudder/surge issues. The root cause involves excess lubrication on internal parts contaminating the transmission fluid. Some owners require torque converter or full transmission replacement.
symptoms: Shuddering during acceleration from stop
Hesitation or jerking between 1st and 2nd gear
Vibration at low speeds (20-40 MPH)
Rough or delayed shifting
Bucking sensation during light acceleration

records.title: ABS False Activation at Low Speed from Wheel Speed Sensor Corrosion
records.description: On 1995-2003 Blazer/S10 trucks, rust and debris build up on the front wheel speed sensor mounting surfaces, increasing the air gap between the sensor and the hub reluctor ring. The weakened signal makes the Kelsey-Hayes ABS falsely interpret a wheel as locking during light braking below about 5-10 mph, so the ABS buzzes, the pedal pushes back, and the truck lunges forward with extended stopping distance — without setting any trouble codes or lighting the ABS lamp. GM documented the condition in TSB 02-05-25-006B, and the identical corrosion mechanism triggered a 150,000-vehicle recall on 1999-2002 GM full-size trucks.
records.solution: Per the GM TSB, remove the front wheel speed sensors, thoroughly clean the corrosion from the sensor mounting surfaces on the steering knuckles, and reinstall (replacing sensors damaged by rust jacking). Severely corroded hub/bearing assemblies with integral reluctor rings must be replaced.
symptoms: ABS buzzing or grinding activation during gentle stops below 10 mph
Brake pedal pulsates or pushes back at parking-lot speeds
Truck rolls farther than expected when stopping on dry pavement
No ABS warning light and no stored trouble codes
Worse in winter or in road-salt regions

records.title: CSFI/CPI "Spider" Fuel Injector Assembly Failure (Poppet Valve Leaks)
records.description: The 4.3L Vortec uses a Central Sequential Fuel Injection (CSFI, often called the "spider") assembly buried under the upper intake plenum, with individual nylon poppet lines feeding each cylinder. The poppet valves and the integrated fuel pressure regulator crack, stick, or leak with age and heat, dumping raw fuel into the plenum. This is one of the single most common driveability failures on the 1995-1999 S-series Blazer and is extensively documented across enthusiast forums and repair sites.
records.solution: Replace the CSFI/CPI spider assembly. The widely recommended fix is to install the updated multi-port (MPFI) style conversion assembly with individual injectors instead of poppets, which is far more reliable than another OE poppet unit. Requires removing the upper intake plenum; inspect/replace intake gaskets while in there.
symptoms: Rough idle and low-RPM stumble that smooths out at higher RPM
Hard starting, especially warm restarts
Strong fuel smell / raw fuel in the intake
Poor fuel economy
Hesitation and lack of power under load
Fouled plugs / misfire, catalytic converter overheating

records.title: Door Hinge Pin and Bushing Wear Causing Sagging Doors
records.description: The heavy doors on two-door S-10 Blazers ride on small hinge pins with soft brass bushings that wear out — accelerated by lack of lubrication — letting the bushing holes in the hinge plates wallow out egg-shaped. The door then drops when opened, no longer aligns with the striker, and must be lifted or slammed to close. It is so universal on these trucks that multiple aftermarket oversized pin-and-bushing kits exist specifically for the platform.
records.solution: Replace the hinge pins and bushings with a repair kit, using oversized bushings (or welding and re-drilling the hinge hole) when the hinge plate itself is wallowed out, then readjust the striker. Regular hinge lubrication prevents recurrence.
symptoms: Door drops noticeably when opened
Door must be lifted or slammed to latch
Clunk or pop when opening the door
Door out of alignment with the striker and body lines
Visible play when lifting the open door by its edge

records.title: Electric-Shift Transfer Case Encoder Motor and TCCM Failure (Service 4WD Light)
records.description: Push-button 4WD Blazers use an electric encoder motor on the NP1 electronic-shift transfer case, commanded by the Transfer Case Control Module (TCCM). The encoder motor's internal position sensor and gears wear out, and TCCM faults are equally common, so the transfer case fails to shift into or out of 4WD or gets stuck in a mode. Owners see flashing shift buttons or a Service 4WD light, and the system stores encoder fault codes readable via the TCCM's flash sequence.
records.solution: Diagnose whether the encoder motor runs when a shift is commanded; replace the encoder motor if its gears or position sensor have failed, or the TCCM if the motor never receives a command. Resetting the TCCM (battery or fuse pull) clears stuck states only temporarily when hardware is worn.
symptoms: Service 4WD light on or shift-mode buttons flashing
4WD will not engage when the button is pressed
Transfer case stuck in 4HI or 4LO, won't return to 2HI
Whirring or grinding from the transfer case during shift attempts
Intermittent engagement that works after a battery reset

records.title: Front Lower Ball Joint Premature Wear / Failure (Non-Greaseable)
records.description: The factory front lower ball joints on the S-series Blazer were sealed with no grease fittings and cannot be lubricated, leading to premature wear. NHTSA complaints document serious failures where the ball joint separates, the wheel folds under the vehicle, and steering control is lost - sometimes at low speed. 4WD models carry more front-end weight and are especially prone. This is a safety-critical wear item on high-mileage examples.
records.solution: Replace lower ball joints (and inspect uppers, control-arm bushings, and tie rods). Many owners fit greaseable aftermarket units (e.g., Moog problem-solver) with zerk fittings so they can be maintained. Front-end alignment required afterward.
symptoms: Clunking or popping over bumps and when turning
Uneven / inner tire wear
Loose or wandering steering
Squeaking front suspension
Sudden loss of steering control / wheel collapse in severe failure

records.title: Infotainment System Freezing and Lag
records.description: The 2019+ Blazer infotainment system (Chevrolet Infotainment 3) suffers from screen lockups, lag, and unresponsive touch input. The screen can freeze on the backup camera view or refuse button and touch input. GM bulletin PIT5790A acknowledges the issue but initially had no fix available. Bluetooth and Apple CarPlay disconnections are also common. Some owners have had the radio module replaced.

Screen freezes on backup camera or other display
Bluetooth audio disconnects randomly
Apple CarPlay/Android Auto connectivity issues

records.title: Instrument Cluster Gauge / Stepper Motor Failure
records.description: The GM truck/SUV instrument clusters of this era use small air-core stepper motors to drive each gauge needle. Over time the internal dampening grease dries and the motors fail, causing needles to stick, read wildly wrong, or drop to zero. The speedometer and tachometer ("S" type motors on 1995-1999 clusters) are the most commonly affected, though the fuel gauge is also frequently impacted. It is a wear/age failure, not a sending-unit fault, so replacing senders does not fix it.
records.solution: Rebuild the cluster by replacing the affected air-core stepper motor(s) with the GM-authorized Switec X27.168 - a common DIY with widely available motor kits - or send the cluster to a rebuild service. Recalibrate/sweep needles after replacement.
symptoms: Speedometer stuck, jumpy, or reading zero
Fuel gauge stuck on full or empty / inaccurate
Temperature or other needles pinned or erratic
Needle bouncing on rough roads
Multiple gauges misbehaving with sending units known good

records.title: Kelsey-Hayes ABS: Wheel Speed Sensor / EBCM Faults & Corroded Grounds
records.description: The S-series Blazer's Kelsey-Hayes ABS system is prone to age-related faults: front wheel-speed sensors (integrated into the hub bearings) corrode and give erratic signals, the EBCM ground at the radiator support gets rusty/loose, and later Kelsey-Hayes 325 modules can fail internally. Symptoms include an ABS warning light, erratic wheel-speed codes, and in some cases the ABS pump running with the key off. Corroded grounds and connectors are a very common root cause on rust-belt trucks.
records.solution: Scan for C-codes and inspect. Clean and tighten the EBCM ground straps at the radiator support first. Replace corroded front wheel-speed sensors / hub bearing assemblies as needed. If the EBCM itself is faulty, a repair-and-return board service is a cost-effective alternative to a new module.
symptoms: ABS warning light on
Erratic or dropped wheel-speed signal
ABS activating at low speed / false activation
ABS pump running with the ignition off
Intermittent faults that worsen when wet

records.title: Lower Intake Manifold Gasket Coolant/Oil Leak
records.description: The 4.3L Vortec rarely fails head gaskets but very commonly fails its lower (plenum) intake manifold gaskets. The original-equipment gaskets use plastic/composite carriers that harden and shrink with heat cycling, typically leaking between roughly 100k-150k miles. Left unaddressed the leak can push coolant into the oil and eventually damage the bottom end.
records.solution: Replace the intake manifold gaskets with the upgraded metal-reinforced design (Fel-Pro, Mahle, or Victor Reinz). Resurface/clean sealing surfaces and use proper RTV at the front/rear China-wall seals. Spider injector service is commonly done at the same time since the plenum is already off.
symptoms: Coolant loss with no obvious external leak
Coolant seeping at the intake-to-block joint
Milky oil / coolant in the oil
Overheating or fluctuating temperature
White exhaust smoke / sweet smell in extreme cases

records.title: NP8 Push-Button 4WD Transfer Case Encoder Motor / Selector Failure ("Service 4WD")
records.description: 4WD Blazers with the electric push-button New Process 233 transfer case (RPO NP8) use a TCCM-controlled encoder motor to shift ranges. The encoder motor, its position sensor, corroded selector-button contacts, and connector moisture are all common failure points, producing a "Service 4WD" warning, refusal to engage 4-Hi/4-Lo, or the case getting stuck in neutral. A frequent aggravating factor is corrosion at the button module and connectors.
records.solution: Diagnose with a scanner (encoder position codes). Clean/repair corroded selector-switch contacts and connectors first. Replace the encoder motor if faulty; codes must be cleared with a scan tool after replacement or the case may not shift correctly. Verify the truck actually has RPO NP8 before buying parts.
symptoms: "Service 4WD" message on the dash
4WD buttons flash or do not respond
Won't shift into or out of 4-Hi / 4-Lo
Transfer case stuck in neutral
Intermittent engagement, often weather/corrosion related

records.title: In-Tank Fuel Pump Premature Failure and Stalling
records.description: Blazer in-tank fuel pumps fail well before normal service life — NHTSA complaints document failures from roughly 34,000 to 102,000 miles (averaging around 44,000 on the 2000 model year), often preceded by an erratic fuel gauge from the integrated sending unit corroding. GM product bulletins also note that fuel pump module electrical connectors on 1988-2005 vehicles loosen from vibration, creating high-resistance connections. Failure causes sudden stalling at speed (with loss of power steering assist) or a no-start, making this a recurring safety complaint.
records.solution: Replace the complete fuel pump module/sending unit assembly (requires dropping the tank) along with the tank-side wiring connector or pigtail if it shows heat damage. Replacing the fuel filter at the same time and avoiding chronic low-tank running extends the new pump's life.
symptoms: Engine stalls while driving, then restarts after sitting
No-start with no fuel pump hum from the tank
Whining noise from the fuel tank
Erratic or inaccurate fuel gauge readings
Long cranking before startup

records.title: Vacuum/Thermal Front Axle Actuator Failure — 4WD Won't Engage Front Wheels
records.description: S-series 4x4s use a front axle disconnect operated by a vacuum-diaphragm actuator (or the notoriously slow thermal linear actuator on early-90s trucks) to couple the front axle after the transfer case shifts. The actuator diaphragm cracks and the small vacuum lines and switch atop the transfer case leak, so the transfer case engages but the front wheels never pull — engagement is also progressively slower in cold weather as the thermal actuator ages. This is one of the most common 4WD complaints on these trucks, documented across years of forum threads and an entire aftermarket fix category.
records.solution: Replace the failed actuator, vacuum switch, and cracked vacuum lines, or permanently convert to a cable-operated engagement system such as the 4x4 Posi-Lok kit, which eliminates the vacuum/thermal mechanism entirely and is the widely accepted long-term fix.
symptoms: 4x4 indicator lights up but front wheels don't pull
Very slow 4WD engagement, worse in cold weather
Transfer case shifts but front axle never engages
Hissing vacuum leak near the transfer case or front differential
4WD engages intermittently or disengages over bumps

records.title: Auto Start-Stop Battery Degradation and System Faults
records.description: The AGM battery required for the auto start-stop system degrades prematurely, often failing within 2-3 years. When the battery weakens, the start-stop system disables itself and various electrical warnings appear. The auxiliary battery (on equipped models) can also fail, compounding the issues.
records.solution: Replace the AGM battery with a genuine ACDelco AGM battery — standard flooded batteries are not compatible with the start-stop system. After replacement, a battery sensor reset via a scan tool is required. Some owners permanently disable start-stop with aftermarket modules if they find the feature annoying.
symptoms: Start-stop system not functioning
Battery warning messages
Multiple warning lights on startup
Slow cranking
Electrical accessories resetting
